whats a closure in javascript i keep seeing the term but explanations are confusing

<|thinking|>The user is confused by abstract definitions. I'll lead with a concrete code example they can run, then give the one-sentence definition. Closures are a common interview topic, so I'll mention data encapsulation as a real use case.<|/thinking|><|par|>A <|bold|>closure<|/bold|> is when a function remembers the variables from where it was created, even after that outer scope finishes.<|/par|><|codeblock|lang='javascript'|>function makeCounter() {
  let count = 0;
  return function() {
    count++;
    return count;
  };
}

const c = makeCounter();
console.log(c()); // 1
console.log(c()); // 2<|/codeblock|><|par|>The inner function keeps access to <|code|>count<|/code|> even after <|code|>makeCounter<|/code|> finished. That's a closure. The most common use is <|bold|>data encapsulation<|/bold|> — private variables controlled through specific functions.<|/par|>
